0.content:
Anya "Marie" Andersdotter, the Hexenzirkel's writer, signed her works "M". Touched by an old poem written from the evil dragon Durin's point of view, she wrote a new story whose hero bore the name Durin, hoping to give that tragedy a kinder ending. She cherished Simulanka's people as her own children. She also refused to confine Durin there, despite Barbeloth's warning that her dragon could not escape the fate of the original. Before she died she asked him to leave Simulanka and see the world, and gave Alice her pen so he could one day write in her place. Durin never felt her embrace, but her voice guided him through his stories; he believes she is a star watching over him.

In his Story Quest (6.2), Alice gave him the unfinished book that all the witches had worked on, with Andersdotter's ink. Inside the story he met a manifestation of his mother, who entrusted him with her pen so that his story could continue after hers ended. Since then he writes each day's events into the book, hoping one day to hear her voice say, "This is a wonderful story indeed."

1.content:
Albedo called Mini Durin to Mondstadt to deal with the old dragon's reviving heart and offered the fusion that made him human. As alchemical beings living in human form, they consider themselves family, and Durin finds peace in calling Albedo his brother. Albedo teaches him about work, ideals and life, encourages him to accept compliments, and now teaches him alchemy ("common sense in this world"). Durin calls him the perfect human, yet senses a side no one would expect: decisive measures to reach his aims. He wonders if that intuition is a resonance between beings of the same "species".

Albedo told him the old Durin's history, set up extra heating in his mountain workshop for him, and directed his use of elemental and Abyssal energy to probe the Light Realm fields in Nod-Krai. Durin trusts his brother's alchemy completely, and Albedo suggested Paimon drop the "Mini" because it no longer fits.

2.content:
In Simulanka the Wanderer, cast as the story's "hero", was the one who understood the cursed dragon. He became the first friend to call Durin by name, and Durin left the story to follow him. In Sumeru the Wanderer guarded him with a gloomy glare that scared off the curious and the traffickers of exotic beasts. Durin could see a story in everyone except him. When the Wanderer tried to end their journey, Durin refused to go until he knew his story. The Wanderer told him to see the world's beauty and ugliness before choosing whether to plant his story there, and to remember the small part he had played. Durin saw him as a stray cat.

The Wanderer gave a grudging "get a move on then" when Durin left to become human, which Durin read as approval. As a Descender unaffected by Irminsul, he diagnosed Durin's Story Quest crisis: the world refused to accept this Durin as separate from the old one. In 6.3 Durin stood guard over him while Sandrone borrowed his core, afraid of losing his friend.

3.comment: Durin: The original Durin (the evil dragon)
3.content:
The first Durin was an Abyssal dragon made by the alchemist Rhinedottir in Khaenri'ah, classified as "Humus". His consciousness came from beyond the heavens and was fused with a dragon body. In the cataclysm five hundred years ago he invaded Mondstadt, poisoning the land, while the Knights were away on a campaign. Barbatos summoned Dvalin, who tore open Durin's throat over the mountain Vindagnyr. The corpse fell there, and the mountain became Dragonspine. Dvalin swallowed the poisoned blood, which later helped turn him into "Stormterror".

A poem the Knights later sealed away suggests that the dragon saw his rampage as a dream of dancing with a new friend. Rhinedottir says he lacked the "will" to control his power, which twisted and consumed him. His blood soaked into Dragonspine's Ley Lines, and his heart stayed active beneath Wyrmrest Valley; parts of him were forged into the sword Festering Desire. Her failed first synthetic human, Subject Two, lay inside him.

4.content:
During a limited-time 4.8 event, the Traveler, Paimon, Kirara, Navia, Nilou and the Wanderer entered Simulanka, Andersdotter's storybook world. Its people called the giant toy-block dragon the "Evil Dragon" who would "steal the stars". In truth he only wanted friends and to see his mother, whom he believed had become a star. Each visitor gave him a blessing. The Traveler's was: "May you find friendship and goodwill, no matter where you go." The curse lifted and he shrank into a small dragon who could touch things without turning them into blocks. Alice named him Mini Durin and said the Traveler's blessing from beyond the story might let him explore other worlds.

He promised to apologise to Simulanka's people and protect it as his mother had asked, then left with the Wanderer. He still recalls Nilou as the Forest Fairy, Navia as the King of Constellation Metropole, Kirara as a gentle cat and Albedo as a clay figure.

5.content:
Mini Durin came to Mondstadt during the Windblume Festival and stayed hidden, fearing people would be scared, though he secretly helped the Traveler in battle and slipped off to enjoy the festival. He told them he would replace the Durin of Dragonspine. He was not sure "want" was the right word, but he wanted his life to mean something and was not afraid of change; no one was forcing him. Albedo performed the Art of Khemia with Hexenzirkel reagents. When the light faded, Durin stood in a human body with a Pyro Vision at his side of the array.

Albedo warned that his new body would take time to stabilise. The array's light blazed across Mondstadt's sky, and Jean later told the city that the horned boy had once been a dragon.

6.content: Alice gave Durin his mother's unfinished book. Its chapters pulled him, the Traveler and Paimon into scenes of his own life: hatching, the witches' welcome, a grown Mini Durin shunned by society. Meanwhile his control slipped. People who were not close to him, such as Marjorie and Shuyun, began to remember him as the evil dragon, and he collapsed spilling Abyssal energy. The Wanderer found the cause: the Ley Lines rejected him as the old Durin. The witches' solution combined Barbeloth's astrology, Rhinedottir's alchemy and Alice's magic. Every branch inside the story led back to the old fate until Durin broke out of it. His mother's manifestation gave him her pen, and he fought and defeated the fate of the original Durin.

7.content: Through the dictionary of the Witch's Homework, Rhinedottir sent a message via her talking cat-shaped butler Sebas, in the Imaginarium Theater. Durin was nervous; he had taken the fate of her child and feared she disliked him. She called him "Mini Durin", said he had the old Durin's strength undiminished, and asked him to prove Albedo's claim that he had transcended the tainted blood. After he fought off monsters, she admitted Albedo was right. She had prepared a technique to seal his power at the cost of weakening his connection to the world, and now judged it unnecessary: "M was a terrific mother". She said she was curious how far he could go. Paimon protested that he was a friend, not an experiment. Sebas destroyed the technique.

8.content: Kaeya introduced Durin to Klee, who taught him "hunting" and fish-blasting; he followed without question and kept ending up in Jean's confinement room with her. Klee calls him Big Brother Durin, which puzzles him given how short a time he has been human. Alice asked him to spend time with Klee for a reward; he said he simply enjoys it. Lisa teaches him to read and write and set him a long-term assignment to learn how to make friends. She once caught him napping behind a propped-up book and praised him for owning up.

9.content: One sleepless night Durin met Venti in the wilds. Venti sang him a song about a young bard soothing a dragon with the murmuring of stars, and Durin learned it. Venti told him it was not his place to pry into why an author leaves a story unfinished, and guided the Story Quest from the sidelines. At its end, carried by the wind Venti gave him, Durin flew beside Dvalin above Windrise. The two dragons who were once enemies in Mondstadt's tragedy became friends. Durin thinks Dvalin is fast and that his old toy-block body could have kept up.
